root_cause.summary: The w30/31 entry churn was NOT a rAthena bug and NOT client-side: it was server-side inter-server disconnection caused by operator container churn. The char-server could not register with the login-server because compose-network DNS (aardvark-dns) resolved peer service names to stale/wrong container IPs after repeated recreate/restart cycles (each restart also reassigns the container IP). With no char-server online, the login accepted credentials (SQL fine) then refused every client with 'Connection refused: there is no char-server online'; clients hung on the map handoff, received no vitals/actors, and looped the 60s stall kick. A secondary effect: pasta port-forwards for recreated containers went stale, so even host-side probes EOF'd before reaching the login.
evidence: journalctl --user: login log '[Notice]: Authentication accepted (account: fx_e09b999a23_0, id: 2000000)' followed immediately by '[Status]: Connection refused: there is no char-server online (account: fx_e09b999a23_0)' and '[Warning]: connect_check: DDoS Attack detected' — the 60s reconnect loop of w30/31 is this refusal cycle

journalctl --user: char-server 'Connecting to 10.89.2.35:6900 ... connect failed (111)' where 10.89.2.35 was the char's OWN IP on the then-current network (DNS self/wrong resolution); map-server dialed its own IP for the char-server likewise
docker inspect: fresh-network recreate produced login=.5 char=.3 map=.4, but the char still dialed .35/.34 = stale network addresses served by the poisoned DNS registry
docker restart reassigns container IPs in this podman network, so literal-IP pins must be (re)applied between restarts

recovery_procedure_that_worked: 1. Enabled server-side console visibility: docker cp conf out, set console_msg_log: 1 (map/char) — NOTE login_athena.conf at this pin does NOT support console_msg_log (login exits 1); instead server console output is visible via journalctl --user (podman journald driver), which was the decisive evidence source
2. docker cp pushes must chmod 644 the file first — a 0600 file owned by the host-mapped uid makes rAthena fail conf load with 'Configuration file not found'
3. compose down (network REMOVED) + up mariadb first, then the three rathena services together — fresh network re-registered DNS but resolutions still returned stale IPs, so:

4. Literal-IP pins applied in dependency order with the PIN-RESTART PIANO: patch char_athena.conf login_ip -> login's current IP, restart char; then patch map_athena.conf char_ip -> char's NEW IP, restart map. The login must be restarted FIRST (fresh pasta port-forward for host clients); it dials nobody so its IP change only requires re-pinning the char before its restart

5. Verified via journal: 'Connection of the char-server RO Bots accepted', 'Map-Server 0 connected: 1265 maps', 'Map Server is now online'; client path verified by the window's own logins: 'Fx_e09b999a23_1 logged in (AID/CID 2000001/150001)' and readback counts 2 1

world_state_after_recovery.fragility: ANY rathena container recreate/restart invalidates the pins and pasta forwards; recovery = re-run the pin-restart piano. Long-term fix (world lane): static IPs in compose or a conf-templating step that injects resolved IPs at start
